Asterid.name: Asterid
Asterid.publicNotes:
Asterids are nymphs of the stars, serene guardians of clear night skies and isolated pockets of the natural world far from the smog and light pollution of mortal cities. They spend their nights sitting in open fields or standing at the crests of high mountains, their heads tilted back to silently watch the stars go by. The rapturous, dreamy expressions asterids wear during their nightly observations have inspired countless works of art on the themes of beauty and longing.

As asterids are bound to general locations rather than specific natural features, they often must rely on alliances and friendships with other kinds of nymphs to find shelter. During the day, asterids generally end up sleeping in the tree-homes of dryads, beneath naiad ponds, or in the courts of their queens. This, alongside the asterids' generally quiet and gentle demeanor, leads many other nymphs to be somewhat protective of them, especially the asterid queens.

Mortals looking to establish an observatory can ask for no better location than one beloved by an asterid, though they would do well to approach such an endeavor with care and diplomacy. Those who come to the nymph with deference and respect the sanctity of the surrounding natural beauty may earn themselves a quiet but attentive guardian, eager to share their knowledge in exchange for the ability to more closely observe their beloved stars. Those who mar the natural world with excess construction or, worst of all, drown out the stars with excess light provoke the asterid's wrath and find their endeavor cursed with misfortune, if not destroyed entirely by the fury of the nymph's protective friends.

action->Starlight Dependent.name: Starlight Dependent
action->Starlight Dependent.description: An asterid is mystically bonded to a single remote location with a good view of the open sky at night, most often a remote island, mountaintop, or open field. If they aren't in that location to see the sky at night on any given day, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}, increasing the value by 1 for each night they miss, with the drained value increasing at sunrise each day. The drained value reduces by 1 only when they see the stars again. The asterid can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond to a new location.

action->Knowledge from the Stars.name: Knowledge from the Stars
action->Knowledge from the Stars.description:
Requirements It's currently night, and the asterid can see the sky

Effect The asterid looks to the stars for guidance and rolls a d20. Until the start of their next turn, they can use the result of their roll in place of making a check or saving throw. The asterid can't use Knowledge from the Stars again for 1 hour.

action->Starbeam.description: Effect The asterid launches a beam of starlight in a @Template[type:line|distance:120]. Creatures in the line take @Damage[5d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save). Creatures who fail their save also become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

action->Starshine.name: Starshine
action->Starshine.description: An asterid's hair and skin always glow with soft starlight, producing 10 feet of dim light and ranging along the same blue-to-red spectrum as natural stars. This is a magical effect that can be suppressed by magical darkness or covered by, for example, a cloak, but never goes out entirely unless the nymph is killed.

Asterid queens reign over entire constellations and clusters of stars reflected in the seas. In practice, they rule mountain ranges, vast swaths of tundra at the Crown of the World, and remote islands far out to sea where the nights are long and dark. Their domains often (though not always) overlap with those of other nymph queens who sheltered the asterid when she was younger and still accumulating power. Asterid queens always remember their friends and return the favors owed with both powerful magic and the divinatory guidance of the stars.

action->(Nymph Queen) Tied to the Land.description:
An asterid queen is intrinsically tied to a vast, remote location with a clear view of the night sky, such as an isolated island or island chain, a mountain range, or an open plain far from the light pollution of civilization.

A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific region. As long as the queen is healthy, the environment is exceptionally resilient, allowing the nymph queen to automatically attempt to counteract any spell that would harm the environment (such as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7yWXx3qC4eFNHhxD]{Blight} ritual), using her spell DC with a counteract rank equal to the highest-rank druid spell she can cast.

When the nymph queen becomes physically or psychologically unhealthy, however, her warded region eventually becomes twisted or unhealthy as well. In that case, restoring the nymph queen swiftly heals the entire region.

Bagman.name: Bagman
Bagman.publicNotes:
Stories abound of fey who steal away people, and many have a grain of truth. No fey embodies the fear in such tales quite like the bagman. These pale, greasy fey are gluttons who delight in eating sentient creatures. They capture their prey within bloody sacks, spiriting them away to murder the victim and devour everything but their fat. That, they save, rendering it into foul alchemical elixirs which they then gleefully sell to the unsuspecting settlement from which they kidnapped their victim.

Bagmen don't need to eat for sustenance, nor do they care for wealth—they merely enjoy spreading suffering. They're masters of disguise and often appear as traveling peddlers of medicinals, wearing deep cloaks and wide-brimmed hats, cruelly offering products to townsfolk crafted from missing loved ones.

The effects of this elixir last for 1 day. Only a bagman can create this elixir using fat extractor.

backpack->Bagman's Sack.name: Bagman's Sack
backpack->Bagman's Sack.description: A bagman's sack functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.jaEEvuQ32GjAa8jy]{Spacious Pouch (Type I)}, except that it can hold only sentient creatures or their remains. After it leaves the bagman's possession, it ejects its contents and becomes a mundane burlap sack. The bag has AC 20, 24 HP (BT 12), and can hold up to two Small creatures or one Medium creature; two Tiny creatures take up the same space as a Small creature. If a bagman's sack is lost or destroyed, they can craft a new one with a week's work.

Effect The bagman makes a sack Strike against a creature in reach. If it hits, the target takes an additional @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage; each creature in the sack also takes this bludgeoning damage.

action->Bag Prey.description:
Requirements The bagman has a Medium or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, is holding their bagman's sack, and their sack isn't full

action->Fat Extractor.name: Fat Extractor
action->Fat Extractor.description: A bagman can use the fat of sentient humanoids to create alchemical elixirs. They can create a single common elixir of 4th level or lower, or any elixir for which they have the formula, from a given creature's fat. This process takes 1 hour. Bagmen always know the formula for the elixir of restored youth.

Bannik.name: Bannik
Bannik.publicNotes:
The bannik is the spirit of the bathhouse—also called the sauna or banya—and resembles a wizened little person with wild hair and nails of pine or fir. While domovois consider themselves to be in charge of a home, banniks are the wisest and most respected of the household spirits. Traditionally, the third steaming of the bath belongs to the bannik and their guests (often other faerie creatures), and to interrupt it is a deadly danger.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.
Bannik.senses: tremorsense (imprecise) within their entire bound bath

action->Boil Alive.name: Boil Alive
action->Boil Alive.description:
Requirements The bannik is in their bound bath

Effect The bannik conjures a plume of superheated steam in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 20 feet. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[6d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic] save). The bannik can't use Boil Alive again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Boil Alive]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Master of the Bath.name: Master of the Bath
action->Master of the Bath.description: A bannik's bathhouse never encounters random accidents, and any mortal that bathes there receives a +2 status bonus to Fortitude saves against disease for 1 week. An unfriendly bannik can invert their blessing—bathers take a –2 status penalty instead. A bannik must spend a week in a place before these benefits occur.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A bannik is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound bath. The bannik can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Tear Off Skin.name: Tear Off Skin
action->Tear Off Skin.description: The bannik makes two claw Strikes against the same target. If both hit and deal damage, the bannik pulls off the creature's skin. The target takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,bleed]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}; if either Strike was a critical success, the target takes @Damage[2d4[persistent,bleed]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} instead.

Baobhan Sith.name: Baobhan Sith
Baobhan Sith.publicNotes:
Undeath is rare in the fey realm of the First World, for that plane's infusion with the raw power of life makes undead uncomfortable at best. Yet a few fey have adopted the vile practices and habits of notorious undead while still being living themselves, as seen in the blood-drinking habits of the murderous baobhan sith.

A baobhan sith avoids confrontations when outnumbered, and although territorial, they won't reveal their true nature to larger groups. They prefer to drink blood from victims they find attractive, and they avoid drinking blood from animals and beasts entirely, as they consider such activities to be uncultured.

Drinking Blood from a victim that's already drained doesn't restore any Hit Points to the baobhan sith but increases the victim's drained value by 1. A victim's drained condition decreases by 1 per week. A blood transfusion, which requires 10 minutes, a successful @Check[medicine|dc:20] check, and sufficient blood or a blood donor, reduces the drained value by 1.

Bogey.name: Bogey
Bogey.publicNotes:
A bogey typically hunts a single creature at a time, usually a small child or elderly person, methodically stalking and tormenting their prey. Often hiding under a bed, amid a dark attic space, or in a closet left slightly ajar, a bogey delights in the slow, methodical cultivation of fear in their victims until the time comes to reap their soul.

Bogeymen are stealers of innocence and devourers of souls. Few targets who survive an encounter with them remain untouched by repeated nightmares, feelings of paranoia, and newly realized phobias. Different names are given to bogeymen according to their varying sizes and degrees of power, which typically grow stronger and stronger as the monsters consume more and more souls.

Many bogeymen look like the mortal folk that they prey on, allowing them to often hide in plain sight.

action->Devour Soul.name: Devour Soul
action->Devour Soul.description:
Requirements The bogey has killed a creature within the last round and is adjacent to its corpse

Effect The bogey consumes the creature's soul. The soul is utterly destroyed—nothing short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic can restore it to life, and only after the bogey has been slain. The bogey regains Hit Points equal to double the level of the consumed creature. After devouring three souls within a year, the bogey transforms into a bugaboo.

Bogeyman.name: Bogeyman
Bogeyman.publicNotes:
These nocturnal stalkers tail their chosen quarry for days, even weeks at a time, ominously showing up in back alleys, shadowy street corners, and even in victims' own homes before going in for the kill. For unfathomable reasons, a bogeyman may spare a victim's life and instead kidnap them, absconding to a far-off location before returning years later with a fresh bogey in tow. The process of creating a new bogey is little understood by mortal occultists, as those who undergo it have little incentive to discuss the procedure and any who witness it become primary targets for the bogeymen who participated in it.

Booted Tom.name: Booted Tom
Booted Tom.publicNotes:
"Don't kick that cat," an elder might warn a young child, "lest you rouse ol' Booted Tom." While most believe the legend of Booted Tom to be just that, a few mortals have received the shock of their lives when they heard a voice whisper, "Pssst, hey you!" and witnessed a feline emerge from the shadows, walking upright and clad in immaculate leather boots.

A booted tom, sometimes referred to in children's tales as a puss in boots, is a restless creature, a master manipulator who finds the maltreated and helps them out of all kinds of trouble, from arranged marriages to imprisonment by abusive caretakers. While the motives of these fey seem benevolent, as with many First World creatures, their methods vary wildly. Sometimes their aid is harmless, yet there's also a tale of an impoverished woman who wished to marry her sweetheart, but her beloved's aristocratic family forbade the match. Her booted tom saw to it that the entire snobby family suffered a series of fatal "accidents," leaving only her beloved alive, free to marry her.

Though the name "booted tom" would imply that such creatures are all male tomcats, in fact, this feline fey can be any gender. Booted toms change form the way mortals change socks. The only thing that remains consistent about their appearance is their very fine, always supple, leather boots.

action->Not the Boots!.description: Booted toms are protective of their boots and seek retribution against anyone who damages or attempts to steal them. In humanoid form, the booted tom is Medium size of any common ancestry, but they must be wearing their signature boots. The booted tom's animal form is a house cat walking on four legs. In animal form, they can still cast ventriloquism, which gains the subtle trait. Their animal form is the only time they're seen without their boots, which meld to their body.

action->Hissed Secrets.name: Hissed Secrets

The target takes @Damage[10d8[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:28|basic] save). The booted tom can't use Hissed Secrets again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Hissed Secrets]]{1d4 rounds}.

Bugaboo.name: Bugaboo
Bugaboo.publicNotes:
The more powerful and sophisticated bugaboo conceals themself within larger darkened spaces to stalk their prey. They might be spotted peering around the corner of a dim hallway only to quickly move out of sight, turn invisible, and attack their victim from an altogether different angle.

Bogeymen are stealers of innocence and devourers of souls. Few targets who survive an encounter with them remain untouched by repeated nightmares, feelings of paranoia, and newly realized phobias. Different names are given to bogeymen according to their varying sizes and degrees of power, which typically grow stronger and stronger as the monsters consume more and more souls.

Many bogeymen look like the mortal folk that they prey on, allowing them to often hide in plain sight.

action->Devour Soul.name: Devour Soul
action->Devour Soul.description:
Requirements The bugaboo has killed a creature within the last round and is adjacent to its corpse

Effect The bugaboo consumes the creature's soul. The soul is utterly destroyed—nothing short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic can restore it to life, and only after the bugaboo has been slain. The bogey regains Hit Points equal to double the level of the consumed creature. After devouring six souls within a year, the bogey transforms into a bogeyman.

action->Mobility.name: Mobility
action->Mobility.description: When the bugaboo uses a Stride action to move half their Speed or less, that movement does not trigger reactions.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The bugaboo deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Striking Fear.name: Striking Fear
action->Striking Fear.description:

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

action->Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
action->Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the bugaboo.

Cat Sith.name: Cat Sith
Cat Sith.publicNotes:
Cat siths can easily pass for common black house cats, noteworthy only for the white spots on their chests and their unusually bristly personalities. In actuality, they're cunning fey, fully capable of speech, trickery, and even walking upright on their hind legs and using their forepaws almost as skillfully as hands. Cat siths live around highland towns and cities, regularly venturing unnoticed into nearby communities by posing as domesticated felines or using magic to take humanoid form. While some cat siths gather information and undertake tasks for more powerful fey creatures, others serve only their own mysterious agendas.

Cat siths are harbingers of misfortune and find amusement in the unluckiness that follows in their wake. Though rarely malicious, they're fascinated by death in all its forms and may go so far as to steal the souls of those already dying for some inscrutable purpose.

Some foolhardy spellcasters attempt to take cat siths as their familiars, hoping to take advantage of their innate power. A cat sith might temporarily pretend to work alongside such a magic user, only to inevitably lead them toward deadly misfortune and capture their soul upon their death. Rarely does a cat sith's goals align with those of a mortal witch who has sworn fealty to a fey patron, and should they join forces, they become a dangerous force to be reckoned with.

action->Steal Soul.description: The cat sith touches a dying creature or the corpse of a creature that died within the past 3 days. While its soul is imprisoned, the creature can't be brought back to life by any means short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic. Choxani.name: Choxani
Choxani.publicNotes:
Known by mortals as "picture people," choxanis are reflections of natural mimicry and resemblance. They embody a chameleon's camouflage, a cloud that resembles a dragon, and all the other ways the natural world reflects upon itself, coincidentally or intentionally. Choxanis see these natural parallels as proof that all reality, from the First World to the Universe and beyond, has a parallel, repeating structure and destiny. Though rarely concerned with the affairs of deities, considering them merely another manifestation of the underlying nature of reality, they honor this structure itself with religious fervor.

Choxanis are humanoid figures with tough, woody skin and shimmering dragonfly wings. They communicate primarily through hand gestures and the colorful markings that cover their bodies, which can change in an instant to form text or images. Their faces are smooth and featureless, and they're unable to speak or eat—instead, they gain sustenance from the hues of other creatures, unfolding the markings off their bodies to siphon color from their prey. While not all choxanis are hostile, their diet makes most mortals wary—anyone can become a colorless gray husk after finding themselves a potential meal. Gnomes especially avoid choxanis, terrified of having their color drained.

While most choxanis are happy to converse peacefully, especially if interesting patterns or colors are given as a gift for them to consume, their mindsets can be difficult to fathom. Coincidental appearances capture their interest much more than important information or imminent danger, and whole communities of choxanis have been lost to natural disasters while noting that the oncoming tsunami or wildfire resembled the structure of a nearby leaf. Of course, in the First World, they know they'll likely be reborn with their memories intact after their journey through the River of Souls, so perhaps they simply consider a beautiful observation to be worth the price of death.

Cu Sith.name: Cu Sith
Cu Sith.publicNotes:
Cu siths are hound-like doorkeepers of remote portals to other planes, particularly portals to the untamed realm of the First World. They're highly territorial and roam the highland moors they call home, constantly on the hunt for any creatures that might intrude. Those that bargain with them for safe passage to or from a portal find cu siths to be vigilant (if strict) escorts, keeping their charges safe from extraplanar threats while ensuring they never veer from the most direct path to their destination. Cu siths are highly proficient hunters that offer a single warning in the form of a terrifying bark. Creatures that refuse to flee upon hearing a cu sith's warning bark risk a quick and brutal death.

Cu siths cut imposing figures; they stand as tall as bulls, covered in intertwining roots, plant matter, and shaggy green-and-white fur that terminates in a long, plaited tail. Their fur around their snouts and ears grows long and their eyes glow with a fiery green light.

Some scholars believe that cat siths and cu siths are two sides of the same mysterious coin. While the feline fey proffers naught but misfortune, their canine counterparts will often provide protection to those in need of it. However, both creatures act on their own interests, not wholly understood by mortalkind. And both are the basis of folk stories told around stony hearths and campfires to warn the listeners of the dangers of the wilder spaces of the world. Though cat siths and cu siths have been seen among the highlands, they're almost never spotted together. Many believe this is because the two are eternal enemies, though none have been able to prove this conjecture.

action->Dooming Bark.name: Dooming Bark
action->Dooming Bark.description:
Any creature within 200 feet of the cu sith that hears their Dooming Bark must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:doomed,inflicts:fleeing,inflicts:frightened] save. A creature in an area that the cu sith can't easily reach—such as a hidden burrow or enclosed building—gets a result one degree of success better than it rolled.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and immune to Dooming Bark for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}; if already frightened, the creature's frightened value increases by 1, and it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Failure As success, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure As success, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing}.

action->Worry Prey.name: Worry Prey
action->Worry Prey.description:
Requirements The cu sith has a Large or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in their jaws

On a miss, the cu sith releases the creature.

Dream Builder.publicNotes: As the gods began to work on the First World in earnest, they created a variety of creatures to handle the smaller tasks. Among these are the dream builders, or byjvilis, small fey who resemble elderly humanoids. A byjvili uses powerful dream energies to create structures of any size within the First World, though they can do so only while they're sleeping. As a result, byjvilis are constantly dozing, only committing to long-term rest when shaping the landscape.

Escorite.name: Escorite
Escorite.publicNotes:
The winged silhouette of a descending escorite makes for a terrifying yet beautiful sight that precedes a gruesome end. This enormous fey moth has a wingspan as wide as 15 feet. Equally intimidating are their fleshless horned skull and eerie tendrils that hang from their abdomen.

Escorites are portents of destruction and embodiments of the end that eventually comes to all things. With desolation as their sole priority, an escorite's mere presence accelerates entropy in the area. They irreversibly ruin their stalking grounds, the lingering dust shed by their wings preventing life from flourishing for generations to come. Ironically, however, they have no immunity to their own powers and live only a few years. They prefer it this way. After all, it's an escorite's calling to teach the inevitability of a permanent end to everything, including the immortal denizens of the First World.

Faun Instigator.publicNotes:
Faun instigators are the brash bullies of their kin.

Fauns are humanoid fey with furry goat legs, tails, and horns of varying sizes. Some fauns have more goat-like faces, while others could be mistaken for humans if viewed from the neck up.

Faun Reveler.publicNotes:
Faun revelers enjoy life to its fullest, tails swishing as they bask in the sun or enjoy ripe fruits from a tree.

Fauns are humanoid fey with furry goat legs, tails, and horns of varying sizes. Some fauns have more goat-like faces, while others could be mistaken for humans if viewed from the neck up.

Fear Eater.name: Fear Eater
Fear Eater.publicNotes:
Fear eaters are malicious fey who revel in causing fear in mortals, using it to grow strange, glowing mushrooms from the bodies of their terrified victims. While they require no sustenance to live, fear eaters consider these emotion-soaked mushrooms to be delicacies of the highest order. A few have established "farms" in remote corners of the First World, where they hold kidnapped mortals captive and regularly harvest their fears, discreetly selling their produce to influential fey.

A fear eater resembles a grotesque caterpillar, lined with several pairs of arms and many stubby legs. They can be found in a variety of colors, and some exhibit iridescent patterns across their elongated torsos, dyed by consumption of their colorful crop. A fear eater almost always carries a hookah bowl strapped to their side or back, from which they continually take deep lungfuls of a miasma made from spores of their fear mushrooms.

Fetch Behemoth.name: Fetch Behemoth
Fetch Behemoth.publicNotes:
A fetch behemoth is much larger than a stalker and forms from the soul of a Large fey or humanoid.

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid creature that exists or existed at one point on the Universe. While there are rumors of fetches who are reflections of beings from other planes, if such exist, they must still be duplicates of a sapient creature. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful person undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while in the First World or in an area significantly influenced by that plane. However, they've also been created by potent entities like the Eldest to torment and vex those who've annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that soul's appearance, they have no true memories of their own. They hold fragments of false remembrances from their source, as if they experienced them in a half-remembered dream—which ensures the fetch is enraged by and jealous of their original.

A fetch is similar in appearance to the creature whose soul spawned them, except that they often possess fey-like features such as pointed ears, plant elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a still-living source must take care to hide these features and manifest a fetch weapon that their living template wields.

When a fetch dies, they fade away along with all of their manifested items into a bloom of plant life, their soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held while alive.

Fetch Stalker.name: Fetch Stalker
Fetch Stalker.publicNotes:
Fetch stalkers form from the souls of Medium or Small fey or humanoids. Small fetch stalkers have the same statistics as the fetch stalker below.

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid creature that exists or existed at one point on the Universe. While there are rumors of fetches who are reflections of beings from other planes, if such exist, they must still be duplicates of a sapient creature. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful person undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while in the First World or in an area significantly influenced by that plane. However, they've also been created by potent entities like the Eldest to torment and vex those who've annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that soul's appearance, they have no true memories of their own. They hold fragments of false remembrances from their source, as if they experienced them in a half-remembered dream—which ensures the fetch is enraged by and jealous of their original.

A fetch is similar in appearance to the creature whose soul spawned them, except that they often possess fey-like features such as pointed ears, plant elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a still-living source must take care to hide these features and manifest a fetch weapon that their living template wields.

When a fetch dies, they fade away along with all of their manifested items into a bloom of plant life, their soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held while alive.

Frog Prince.name: Frog Prince
Frog Prince.publicNotes: Lo and behold the tale of the frog prince, often depicted as a lost royal transformed by vile machinations. His daring, amphibious exploits are all in search of the destined love who'll elevate him to his true form and his rightful place upon the throne—or so it goes. When such stories persist in a region, whether as folk tales about a nearby pond or as placation for excitable children before bedtime, the innocent belief in their plight seemingly invokes an inexplicable, ancient power that gives form to frog princes. These fey appear as unusually large frogs, gifted with a capacity for expression atypical for most amphibians.

action->Watery Demesne.name: Watery Demesne
action->Watery Demesne.description: The frog prince designates an unclaimed body of water (typically a pond) to become his demesne. While in his demesne, the frog prince can speak and gains a +15-foot status bonus to all his Speeds. If the frog prince dies or finds a new demesne, the waters turn murky and putrid for 1 week before returning to normal as it ceases to be his demesne.

action->How Dare You!.name: How Dare You!
action->How Dare You!.description:
Trigger A creature misses a Strike against the frog prince

Effect The frog prince makes a melee Strike against the triggering creature if it's within range.

action->Princely Monologue.name: Princely Monologue
action->Princely Monologue.description:
Requirements The frog prince is in his watery demesne

Effect The frog prince enraptures all those who play audience to his speech. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] saving throw. The monologue lasts until the end of the frog prince's next turn, but he can Sustain it for up to 10 minutes. Each time he Sustains the monologue, any creature in the area who hasn't already attempted a saving throw against Princely Monologue must attempt the saving throw.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Princely Monologue for 1 hour.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} with the frog prince, but only for 1 round.

Failure The creature is fascinated with the frog prince and can't willingly move away from the frog prince while it can hear the Princely Monologue.

Critical Failure As failure, except the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} while it can hear the frog prince's Princely Monologue.

action->True Love's Bond.name: True Love's Bond
action->True Love's Bond.description:
Frequency once per year

Trigger A humanoid creature who truly loves the frog prince kisses him

Effect The frog prince permanently transforms into a Small or Medium humanoid. He chooses his ancestry and the details of his appearance, and his equipment changes to suit his new form. The frog prince loses the fey trait and gains the humanoid trait. He has a land Speed of 25 feet and loses his swim Speed. He can use his rapier and water jet Strikes as normal. If the GM determines the humanoid creature's feelings aren't true love, this ability has no effect.

Gathlain Wanderer.name: Gathlain Wanderer
Gathlain Wanderer.publicNotes:
Many gathlains leave the trees of their birth to seek lives of exploration and adventure, some even finding portals to the Universe along their travels.

Gathlains have made a name for themselves as inquisitive and mischievous, as well as flighty and distractable. These eccentric little fey want nothing more than to explore the many wonders of the world for their own pleasure.

Born of magical trees in seed pods that float hundreds of miles on the wind, gathlains are a bizarre mix of flesh and flora. Sprigs of mistletoe bloom from their back and form a delicate pair of wings. They enjoy adorning themselves with oddities found on their journeys, such as beads, pieces of fine cloth, and bits of armor. The fey see these accessories as trophies, proof of their travels, and mementos of their adventures.

The typical gathlain is only 2 feet tall, but their small size doesn't deter them from seeking out and exploring potentially dangerous places. They sometimes even use their size to their advantage, squeezing through tight spaces that most would never be able to fit through. Moreover, their vine-laced wings let them reach heights many adventurers would find daunting. These traits have made them celebrated explorers whose presence is welcome in a group of travelers—as long as everyone is prepared for their nigh-endless questions. A conversation with a gathlain can feel more like an interrogation, as they care little for the comfort of others if it means they will learn something new and interesting to add to their store of knowledge.

Gathlains are particularly fond of gnomes, as they feel a sort of familial attachment to their exiled fey kin, and they usually attempt to ingratiate themselves with any gnomes they run across. Gnomes don't always return this affection, and many tend to distrust gathlains due to the smaller creatures' gossipy and flighty nature.

action->Final Jape.name: Final Jape
action->Final Jape.description: When the gathlain dies, their wings explode into a cloud of toxic mist. Each creature within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] takes @Damage[2d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:17|basic] save).

action->Forest Passage.name: Forest Passage
action->Forest Passage.description: The gathlain ignores difficult terrain caused by plants and fungi, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth.

action->Rootbound.name: Rootbound
action->Rootbound.description:
Requirements The gathlain isn't using their wings to fly

Effect The gathlain sprouts woody roots from the tips of their wings that bind an adjacent creature's limbs. The target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the gathlain's wing-tip vines until the start of the gathlain's next turn.

Gerbie.name: Gerbie
Gerbie.publicNotes:
A lone traveler strays into the woods and stumbles across a circle of mushrooms that tower overhead like trees, each one hollowed out and marked with holes. Numerous pairs of oversized, circular eyes suddenly glow from within the hollows. Within moments, a crowd of small, furry bipeds swarms the wanderer, each resembling a hybrid between a mouse and lizard. And then… the gerbies begin chattering in squeaky, high-pitched voices, bombarding the newcomer with greetings and questions. All welcoming, all smiling, all happy to meet a new friend!

Gerbies live in quaint, communal societies where they craft all their material needs and practice vegetarianism. Knowing that not all places have the privilege of such harmony, gerbies make it their life's purpose to foster peace and friendship wherever they go. Gerbies value empathy and positive communication, and with their natural knack for both, they often appoint themselves as mediators for any conflicts in their vicinity. Conveniently, all it takes is a touch of magical persuasion—and in severe cases, memory modification—to resolve most disputes. Even without their mind-affecting powers, gerbies possess exceptionally pleasant smiles and exude disarming affability.

action->All My Favorite Things!.description:
The gerbie overloads the mind of a creature within 100 feet with thoughts of sunny days, of cute fauna and beautiful flora, of frolicking in fields, and of many other pleasant things. The creature takes @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

action->Forget Now.description: The gerbie attempts a jaws Strike. If the Strike hits, the gerbie affects the creature they just attacked with Make it All Better to make it forget the attack.

action->Make it All Better.name: Make it All Better

Goodfellow.name: Goodfellow
Goodfellow.publicNotes:
Every royal court needs a fool, both to entertain and to humble the mighty with the blade of cutting wit. Among the nobles of the First World, the fey most favored to fill this important role are the charming, mischievous goodfellows. Their favorite targets for pranks are mortals they deem "too uptight." Fey nobles fully expect they, too, will be targets of pranks, though goodfellows wisely keep these on the harmless side. That said, their chaotic whims might strike at any time, and they can't be fully trusted with anything but mischief.

Goodfellows average around 4 to 5 feet tall, with skin that ranges from red to brown and full heads of wild, feathery hair that run a similar spectrum.

Green Knight.name: Green Knight
Green Knight.publicNotes:
Consider a lord on a festival day, fair-faced and merry in his cups, extending his largess to any who please him. Consider that lord on a harvest day, a tyrant in the fields, demanding work he would not do himself. Consider that lord on his commendation day, swearing to protect and nurture the lands and its people in exchange for fealty and troth from those very same subjects.

Consider a green knight, great and green of skin and green of armor, who might appear on such a day to that lord.

The green knights are avatars of honor and of one's word given and kept. They're duty-bound to ensure others, especially those of high station, hold true to the promises they make. Sallying forth from their keeps in the depths of the First World, the green knights arrive anywhere nobility falters: where a lord forgets his vassal vows, a knight wavers in her cause, or an oath maker finds themself on the path of betrayal, a green knight arrives to test their worth. They serve as self-appointed judge, jury, and sometimes executioner, offering boons to those who pass their tests and banes for those who fail.

The greatest among the green knights answer to Magdh herself, who sends them forth to judge and guide mortals who find themselves at such crossroads. Some answer to different Eldest or to older and stranger powers, and others follow only their own codes. Even those green knights who swear no fealty to a higher power, however, have the uncanny ability to find those most deserving of their judgment.

Green knights tower over those they challenge, standing 8 feet tall or more and wearing thick green armor that makes them seem larger still. Despite their intimidating presence, they're genteel and graceful, with perfectly coiffed hair, elegantly trimmed beard, and flawless etiquette. They invariably carry massive bronze axes, symbols of their station, but—as courtly graces demand—they rarely brandish their weapons unless faced with harm. However, should someone be foolhardy enough to challenge a green knight to martial combat, they might find their head quickly and cleanly severed from their body with one mighty blow from that axe.

weapon->Gallant Axe.description: This large battle axe is too heavy to wield with only one hand. Many greataxes incorporate two blades, and they are often "bearded," having a hook at the bottom to increase the strength of their chopping power.

action->Courtly Judgment.name: Courtly Judgment

Effect The green knight returns to life with full Hit Points, points at the creature responsible for their death, and vanishes, returning to the First World. The green knight immediately targets them with the triggering attack or spell as a free action, either immediately or as soon as the target is within range. The attack or spell uses the same attack modifier, save DC, damage, and any other effects as the triggering effect, but the green knight gets a result on their attack roll one degree of success better than they rolled or the target gets a result on their save one degree of success worse than they rolled.

action->Courtly Game.name: Courtly Game
action->Courtly Game.description:
Frequency once per year and a day

Effect The green knight offers a test to a creature they can see, challenging them to live up to their ideals. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35] save. If they fail, they must choose one of two paths.

If the target and the green knight are both still alive 14 days later, the green knight appears before them and offers a reward.

  • Fallen Knight The target strays from its path, possibly falling from grace. For the next year and a day, the target must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5] before using any ability granted by a class, archetype, or other feature that imposes edicts or anathema. On a failure, the ability has no effect. If the target's abilities don't rely on upholding edicts or anathema (or that target has no edicts or anathema), the target instead takes a –1 penalty to Will saves for the duration. In addition, the green knight can communicate telepathically with the creature for the duration, regardless of distance, as long as both are in either the First World or the Universe.

action->Cry of Challenge.name: Cry of Challenge
action->Cry of Challenge.description:

Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:34] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the green knight for 1 minute. action->Gallant Axe.name: Gallant Axe
action->Gallant Axe.description: The green knight's axe is the symbol of their power and judgment. action->Pronounce Judgment.name: Pronounce Judgment

action->Whirling Blow.name: Whirling Blow
action->Whirling Blow.description: The green knight makes a melee Strike against each creature within reach. These attacks count towards the green knight's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the green knight makes all their attacks.

Gremlin Swarm.name: Gremlin Swarm
Gremlin Swarm.publicNotes:
Most gremlins are communal creatures, dwelling in gangs, mobs, and hives just out of mortal sight. These groups are often contentious, each gremlin believing they are taking advantage of the rest, yet they never live alone if they can help it.

On occasion, an entire mass of gremlins can be roused to anger. Such a swarm is surprisingly coordinated and effective, driven not by any one gremlin's leadership but by their excellent instincts for causing trouble. Gremlin swarms cooperate easily to bring down much larger foes, trussing them up like a holiday goose or poking them with knives and claws until they stop twitching.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.

action->Absolute Nuisances.name: Absolute Nuisances
action->Absolute Nuisances.description: 5 feet. The gremlin swarm constantly harasses nearby creatures to break their concentration, kicking shins and screaming in ears. A creature in the aura taking a concentrate action, must first succeed at a @Check[will|dc:18|options:area-effect] save or lose the action. Creatures occupying the gremlin swarm's space take a –2 circumstance penalty to this save.

action->Clever Little Monsters.name: Clever Little Monsters
action->Clever Little Monsters.description:
Frequency once per round

The swarm can use their Thievery ( [[/act disarm skill=thievery]], [[/act grapple skill=thievery]], [[/act shove skill=thievery]], or [[/act trip skill=thievery]]) modifier, rather than Athletics, for the skill check for this action.

action->Grem-a-pult.description:

Each creature in a @Template[type:burst|distance:5] within 30 feet takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). A creature who critically fails the save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round. The gremlin swarm then loses @Damage[1d4[healing]|options:area-damage] Hit Points as the gremlin scuttles back injured.

action->Swarming Blows.name: Swarming Blows
action->Swarming Blows.description: Each enemy in the mob's space takes @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). A creature that fails this save is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Grit Flinger.name: Grit Flinger
Grit Flinger.publicNotes:
These pink- and peach-furred fey resemble large bipedal meerkats. They often wear simple clothes and bands of gemstones wrapped with string and leather. These gems are elegantly cut in the shapes of lizards, scorpions, and desert blooms. Grit flingers possess an innate ability for controlling sand and carry a magical sack of endless sand they use to augment their talents. They tend to live in small communities with expansive tunnel networks deep below ground, typically beneath deserts and badlands.

These resilient fey are believed to guard deposits of precious materials, such as of gemstones, silver, and the purest of iron. The easiest way to anger a grit flinger is to dig near their homes. Upon discovering a hole or tunnel, they'll use their endless sandy sack to fill it in. They then summon a giant sandstorm to scare off any remaining creatures, transforming the landscape into a desert as a warning for any who might think of excavating there.

action->Sack of Sand.name: Sack of Sand
action->Sack of Sand.description: A grit flinger's bag is filled with infinite sand that they can use to beset their foes. The grit flinger can use their abilities with the earth trait only if they're holding an intact sack of sand in one hand. The sack can be targeted by Strikes (AC 27). If the sack of sand takes at least 15 piercing or slashing damage from a single Strike, it starts to leak. At the start of each of the grit flinger's turns, the leaking bag spills sand in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5], creating difficult terrain that lasts for 1 day. The grit flinger can repair the sack with 1 minute of work. If the sack is separated from the grit flinger, it loses its magic and becomes a mundane sack of sand.

action->Wrathful Sands.name: Wrathful Sands
action->Wrathful Sands.description: 10 feet. A cloud of sand surrounds the grit flinger. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the aura takes @Damage[4d6[slashing]] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:24|basic] save. The grit flinger can activate or deactivate the aura with a Sustain action. If the grit flinger's sack of sand starts leaking, the aura ends.

action->Blinding Sand.name: Blinding Sand
action->Blinding Sand.description: A creature hit by the grit flinger's sand slash becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

action->Disseminating Scurry.name: Disseminating Scurry
action->Disseminating Scurry.description: The grit flinger Strides up to half their Speed, spreading sand and gravel into the air while subtly guiding it into annoying nooks and crannies. Each creature the grit flinger moves adjacent to while scurrying must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:26] save as debris lodges uncomfortably under armor, in shoes, or up noses. On a failure, the creature becomes covered in sand until it spends an action shaking off the debris. Anytime a creature covered in sand attempts an action with the concentrate trait, the action is disrupted unless the creature succeeds at a @Check[flat|dc:5].

Harmona.name: Harmona
Harmona.publicNotes:
Catching a glimpse of a harmona is said to be lucky. Flying quickly, these brightly colored avian fey are all but hidden to the naked eye. A soft buzz, discernible only to creatures with particularly keen hearing, accompanies them as they observe and scout places where they might find new sources of food.

Intelligent and curious, these tiny fey birds freely roam the First World, accompanying high-ranking fey creatures like queens or their courts. In turn, companions who treat a harmona with respect for their knowledge and skill benefit from the harmona's aid in times of need.

When these curious creatures find a natural gate between the planes, they glide through to explore and expand their knowledge. Those who find their way onto the Universe often choose to remain there in search of diverse and unusual places. This frequently leads them to the same locations that draw curious adventurers. A harmona might befriend a non-fey adventurer as a companion, but they resent those who would treat them as pets and fight to the death to avoid capture.

Hobkins.name: Hobkins
Hobkins.publicNotes:
Hobkins are eerie little creatures, pallid humanoids with enormous, lantern-like eyes and massive ears on a too-big head. Unlike other gremlins, hobkins aren't fully in step with the Universe. Instead, they're trapped halfway between it and the First World—eternally out of phase, just a hair's breadth from reality. They move strangely, with jerking, jittery gestures that jump between too fast and too slow, and they float above the ground. They have a physical form, but they feel off to the touch, with a texture not quite like anything else.

Where most gremlins dismantle machines or relationships, hobkins love to scare people, striving to spread paranoia and terror wherever they go. A hobkins might lurk outside a child's window during a storm, pressing its great gleaming eyes against the glass until a lightning flash illuminates its horrible visage—and then vanish before the next lightning strike, giggling to itself with delight.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.

action->Not Where You Think.name: Not Where You Think
action->Not Where You Think.description:
Trigger A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} creature misses the hobkins with a Strike

Effect The hobkins redirects the triggering attack to the required creature. The attacker rerolls the attack against the new target.

action->Floating.name: Floating
action->Floating.description: Hobkins always levitate about an inch off the ground, ignoring difficult terrain unless it would also affect flying creatures. House Spirit Mob.name: House Spirit Mob
House Spirit Mob.publicNotes:
Even the smallest house spirits can band together against a threat to the home.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A house sprit mob is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound area. The house spirit mob can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Uncooperative Surroundings.name: Uncooperative Surroundings
action->Uncooperative Surroundings.description: 30 feet. The house spirit mob rallies household items to hamper their foes. Each enemy in the aura that fails an attack roll, Reflex saving throw, or Acrobatics or Athletics skill check becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} on a critical failure).

action->Swarming Blows.name: Swarming Blows
action->Swarming Blows.description: Each enemy in the mob's space takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic] save).

action->Tragic Accident.name: Tragic Accident

The area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute, and the damage is most often bludgeoning. The mob can't use Tragic Accident again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Tragic Accident]]{1d4 rounds}.

Huldra.name: Huldra
Huldra.publicNotes:
At first glance, a huldra seems like a simple creature—a human in plain robes or peasant dress, sporting long hair. These tresses and full skirts in fact disguise the huldra's supernatural features: a hollow wooden back, a long bovine tail, and incredible strength.

Folk legends from the lands of the north describe huldras as the creations of troll witches, intended to lure potential meals to the slaughter. Indeed, a huldra's regeneration is so similar to a troll's that a link between the two creatures seems entirely possible, but huldras despise trolls and resent tales suggesting any connection between them. Rather, huldras are wardens of the woodlands they occupy. Grown from saplings by powerful forest-dwelling fey as a response to humanoid encroachment, huldras protect and parley for the forest itself. Woodland creatures adore huldras and sometimes approach humans or elves thinking they're huldras. This illusion is shattered if the animal sees the humanoid's back is made of flesh or that they're lacking a tail.

Huldras respond well to travelers who show respect and deference for the forest, bestowing those they favor with supernatural luck and fortune. Those who scorn or attack a huldra, or those who mock their distinctive, bovine tails, find themselves plagued by poor decisions and even worse luck. Huldras commonly carry a bad reputation as sirens of the deep forest—cunning monsters who seek to lure woodcutters and unwary adventurers to uncertain ends. These stories largely come from miscreants foolish enough to have treated a huldra rudely and later complain about how they were unjustly persecuted. Even woodcutters and hunters can stay in the good graces of huldras provided they plant new trees to replace what they've taken and don't kill any creatures they don't eat.

Though huldras choose to appear unassuming, their awareness is sometimes lacking when it comes to their strength. They often perform feats of strength, like bending horseshoes straight or lifting heavy objects, without realizing they're breaking their carefully crafted facade.

action->Befuddling Lash.description: When the huldra damages a creature with their tail, a wave of befuddlement clouds the target's thoughts. Hungersome Wolf.name: Hungersome Wolf
Hungersome Wolf.publicNotes:
A hungersome wolf is a fearsome beast who stalks the forests of the First World, following after their prey with silent steps and unending patience. They're known to choose a target and bide their time, finding out the target's usual routes and routines, eventually identifying the perfect time and place to strike. When the moment is right, the wolf will enter into the home of the target, consume one of their loved ones, and shift into that victim's form, waiting for the target to return and become the perfect dessert to their vicious meal.

A hungersome wolf prefers the prey they find in the First World, but occasionally, one finds their way into the Universe. The resulting carnage inspires many stories whispered in the dark of night to children as a warning—against leaving the trail, against leaving an unprotected loved one alone, and most importantly, a warning to trust your instincts.

action->Better to See You With.name: Better to See You With
action->Better to See You With.description: The wolf's keen sense of sight can see through both mundane and magical hindrances when they have their sights set on their prey. The wolf ignores their prey's concealment if they're visible. If their prey is invisible, the wolf treats their invisibility as concealment instead.

action->Run If You Can.name: Run If You Can
action->Run If You Can.description:
Trigger A creature within reach of the wolf's jaws attempts to move out of reach

Effect The hungersome wolf attempts a jaws Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, they disrupt the triggering creature's move action.

action->Stalk Prey.name: Stalk Prey
action->Stalk Prey.description:
The hungersome wolf designates a single sapient creature they can smell and hear as their prey. The hungersome wolf gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [[/act seek]] their prey and Survival checks to [[/act track]] their prey. The wolf gains an additional reaction each round they can use only for Run If You Can against their prey.

If the wolf uses Stalk Prey again, any creature they'd designated as their prey is no longer their prey.

action->You Are What You Eat.name: You Are What You Eat
action->You Are What You Eat.description: This functions as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.eQM5hQ1W3d1uen97]{Change Shape}, except the hungersome wolf must transform into the last creature they Swallowed Whole. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning). The transformation lasts until the hungersome wolf takes 20 or more damage from a single ability, attack, or spell.

Jabberwock.name: Jabberwock
Jabberwock.publicNotes:
Few beasts have inspired as many legends, poems, songs, and myths, in as many cultures, as this bizarre draconic creature. Jabberwocks hail from the fey realm of the First World and are part of a group of powerful First World creatures known collectively as the Tane: living weapons for a war beyond mortal comprehension. Jabberwocks were among the first of the Tane, their kind making up one of the Five Beasts of Ending.

Like all members of the Tane, jabberwocks are living creatures who age, eat, drink, and sleep, but they don't reproduce normally. Instead, they're created directly by the godlike Eldest who rule the First World, and they serve at the pleasure (or frustration) of these capricious and mysterious entities. Believed to be the most powerful of all the Tane, jabberwocks are typically only ever created with one purpose: to wreak destruction and havoc upon the Universe. One of the Eldest might send a jabberwock to devastate a country, continent, or even entire world just to get revenge for some slight made against them by a single mortal. Sometimes, no specific insult or injury is required, as some of the Eldest resent the very existence of the Universe and periodically create jabberwocks simply to express the wrath of the First World against its younger, less chaotic sibling.

Once a jabberwock arrives in the Universe, their first order of business is to seek out a lair. They prefer dwelling in remote forest locations about a day's flight from civilization—the more dangerous the woodland to those who eventually come hunting them, the better!

The relationship between jabberwocks and vorpal weapons is the subject of much debate and speculation among scholars, and the various poems, songs, and legends about jabberwocks do little to clarify the issue, conflicting and diverging on this point. Some believe that vorpal weapons were first created specifically to combat jabberwocks, but others take the story a step further. Certain ancient myths hold that there might once have been only a single, unique jabberwock, so powerful that nothing could so much as scratch them—nothing, that is, except for the first vorpal sword, crafted for that very purpose. So epic was the resulting battle that it created strange echoes throughout reality, and as a result, these echoes, in the form of vorpal weapons, can now be found on many worlds. Those who subscribe to this belief claim that the jabberwocks seen today are but pale imitations of this proto-jabberwock, and they speculate that only the combined efforts of several Eldest would be sufficient to create such a creature again.

Variant Jabberwocks

The Eldest have sometimes altered certain aspects of the jabberwocks they create. Some of the more notorious or legendary variant jabberwocks include the following.

Frumious Jabberwock: Frumious jabberwocks have two heads instead of one. They are 24th level and gain an extra action on each of their turns they can use only to make a jaws Strike.

Mimsy Jabberwock: Typically hailing from wintry regions of the First World, mimsy jabberwocks have glowing blue-white scales, resist cold instead of fire, and have eyes that burn with blue flames that deal cold damage instead of fire damage.

Slithy Jabberwock: Wreaking destruction beneath the waves, these sinuous jabberwocks are amphibious, have a swim Speed of 80 feet instead of the normal fly Speed, and don't have a wing Strike. A slithy jabberwock's Whiffling aura is activated whenever they Swim, make a tail Strike, or Burble.

action->Whiffling.description:

These winds move outward from the jabberwock, and they persist until the start of the jabberwock's next turn. During this time, flight of any kind in the emanation requires a successful [[/act maneuver-in-flight dc=43]]{Acrobatics} check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Qf1ylAbdVi1rkc8M]{Maneuver in Flight}, and creatures flying toward the jabberwock are moving through greater difficult terrain. Creatures on the ground in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:43|name:Approach Jabberwock] check to approach the jabberwock.

Jack-o’-Lantern.name: Jack-o’-Lantern
Jack-o’-Lantern.publicNotes:
These fey creatures appear as road-worn travelers with a coin purse and flask at their belt, carrying a staff bearing a turnip with a glowing, grinning face. When wandering the road at night, should you see a figure holding up a lantern in the distance, take care—it could be a jack-o'-lantern.

Legends say the original Jack of the Lantern was a greedy trickster who fooled a beggar out of his last silver coin. To punish him, an archon cursed the coin so that any who held it would be rooted in place until released by the coin's owner. Luckily for Jack, he already had the coin in his purse and avoided the curse.

When a powerful devil later tried to bargain for Jack's soul, Jack left the shining coin on the table. The greedy devil couldn't resist it and was rooted to the ground for years, causing a bloody revolution in the devil's holdings in Hell.

When Jack died, Heaven refused him on principle, and Hell refused him out of embarrassment, leaving his restless soul to wander. Amused at Jack's antics, the Lantern King placed a speck of his own essence into a carved turnip, offering the implement of power to Jack in return for his eternal service. Ever since, echoes of Jack—jack-o'-lanterns—have roamed the planes at the Lantern King's command, spreading chaos and trickery.

weapon->Lantern Staff.name: Lantern Staff
weapon->Lantern Staff.description: This long piece of wood can aid in walking and deliver a mighty blow.

action->Lantern Allure.name: Lantern Allure
action->Lantern Allure.description: 60 feet. Any creature in the aura that can see the jack-o'-lantern's lantern staff and is in darkness or dim light must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the light for 1 minute. Regardless of the result, the creature is then temporarily immune to this aura for 24 hours.

action->Snuffed Out.name: Snuffed Out
action->Snuffed Out.description: A jack-o'-lantern whose lantern staff is doused with water or otherwise extinguished takes @Damage[3d6[persistent,mental]] damage, which they automatically recover from when they reignite their lantern. While the flame is snuffed out, the jack-o'-lantern can't use their lantern fire Strike, and their lantern staff Strike doesn't deal fire damage.

action->Heavy Coin.name: Heavy Coin
action->Heavy Coin.description: Any creature that accepts or steals the coin from a jack-o'-lantern's purse must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:30] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 10 minutes. A creature that fails its save can attempt a new Will save every minute and the first time each round that it takes damage. The jack-o'-lantern can Dismiss this effect.

action->Spit Summons.name: Spit Summons
action->Spit Summons.description:
Frequency once per day

Requirements The jack-o'-lantern is holding or carrying their flask

Effect The jack-o'-lantern sips from their flask and spits on the ground. The liquor ignites and animates as it leaves their mouth, summoning a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.pVbggIyXxCo8pPue]{Living Wildfire} that also has the fey trait.

Jubjub Bird.name: Jubjub Bird
Jubjub Bird.publicNotes:
A jubjub bird resembles a giant dodo with long, muscular legs and wings capable of brief, if awkward, flight. When attacked with magic, their brilliant plumage, normally purple, shifts randomly in hue and pattern with each spell that hits home.

Jubjub birds belong to the Tane, a group of powerful creatures brought into existence as living weapons by the Eldest. Jubjubs have the dubious reputation of being the least powerful and intelligent of the Tane, though they're still formidable enough that few who underestimate them live long enough to regret the mistake.

Though these birds are sometimes kept as guardians or mounts, the Eldest generally create them for a singular purpose: to be hunted. Just threatening enough to provide a sporting challenge for the high fey lords, once they've been brought down, they make a delicious prize. Their cooked meat is famously exquisite, especially fermented for a few months in mahogany or ivory jars. Mortals who participate in such hunts, however, should take care if they're offered a portion of the prize—certain fey enjoy adding unusual seasonings, including, but not limited to, sawdust, glue, and locusts.

action->Planar Acclimation.name: Planar Acclimation
action->Planar Acclimation.description: The jubjub bird always treats the plane it's on as its home plane.

action->Adaptive Defense.name: Adaptive Defense
action->Adaptive Defense.description:
Trigger The jubjub bird is damaged by an attack that deals cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage

Effect The jubjub bird takes damage as normal, then gains resistance 20 to the triggering damage type for 1 round. If the triggering attack dealt more than one of the listed damage types, the jubjub bird gains resistance 20 to each of them.

action->Perpetual Passion.name: Perpetual Passion
action->Perpetual Passion.description: Jubjub birds grow more frenzied and dangerous as their situation becomes more desperate. The first time the bird's Hit Points are reduced below half of its maximum HP (170 HP), it gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its AC and attack rolls. The first time its Hit Points are reduced below a quarter of its maximum HP (85 HP), the bonus increases to +2, and its Strikes deal an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

action->Scream Shrill and High.name: Scream Shrill and High
action->Scream Shrill and High.description:
The jubjub bird rends the sky with a shrill note like a pencil on a slate. Non-Tane creatures within 120 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:40] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is startled by the cry and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and is momentarily frozen with fear, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and is immobilized for as long as it remains frightened.

action->Sprint.name: Sprint
action->Sprint.description: The jubjub bird Strides three times in a straight line.

action->Sudden Charge.name: Sudden Charge
action->Sudden Charge.description: The jubjub bird Strides twice. If it ends its movement within melee reach of at least one creature, it can make a melee Strike against that creature.

Kaztili.name: Kaztili
Kaztili.publicNotes:
Though always dressed like they're attending the finest court functions, a kaztili behaves more like the patron of an ale hall. Consummate comedians and witty debaters, these liminal sprites love ambages and flyting. Though to outsiders, their interests might seem align with those of murxies, most kaztilis look down on such fellows, considering them low-brow hacks, though others cultivate eager followings of the weaker fey. Kaztilis appear as miniature elves, but with angular, gossamer wings sprouting from their backs.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."
Kaztili.saveDetails: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Comedic Versatility.name: Comedic Versatility
action->Comedic Versatility.description: A kaztili can use Performance for all Deception and Intimidation actions.

action->Witty Repartee.name: Witty Repartee
action->Witty Repartee.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The kaztili speaks a sharp remark about its current situation, emboldening its friends or debilitating its foes. The kaztili attempts a @Check[performance|against:will] check against the Will DC of a creature within 30 feet. On a success, the kaztili chooses to give that creature either a +1 status bonus or –1 status penalty to the next attack roll or skill check it makes before the start of the kaztili's next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.ZPbG3y9LTCI9srmk]{Effect: Witty Repartee}

Kikimora.name: Kikimora
Kikimora.publicNotes:
According to folklore, the kikimora was once a swamp or forest spirit that came to prefer living in a peasant's home to dwelling out in the muck and cold. They look rather like the people they live alongside but sometimes have animalistic features.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.
Kikimora.senses: tremorsense (imprecise) within their entire bound home

action->Master of the Hearth.name: Master of the Hearth
action->Master of the Hearth.description: A kikimora often shares custody of a home with a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.AzYYP23uGecb0Jmw]{Domovoi}. When the two agree, the circumstance bonus or penalty the domovoi provides to checks to Craft, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.QyzlsLrqM0EEwd7j]{Earn Income}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.bT3skovyLUtP22ME]{Repair}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsist} in the home increases to +3 or –3, depending on their shared mood. When the domovoi and the kikimora disagree, all such checks always take a –1 circumstance penalty from the dispute. A kikimora must spend a week in a place before these benefits occur.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A kikimora is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound home. The kikimora can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Home Guardian.name: Home Guardian
action->Home Guardian.description: By commanding their home to attack, the kikimora can [[/act disarm skill=household-lore]], [[/act grapple skill=household-lore]], [[/act reposition skill=household-lore]], [[/act shove skill=household-lore]], or [[/act trip skill=household-lore]] with their enraged home Strike. The kikimora uses their Household Lore instead of Athletics skill for these checks.

action->Unravel.name: Unravel
action->Unravel.description: The kikimora attempts a claw Strike against a creature that's wearing clothing made of fabric. If it hits, the creature's clothing starts to come apart. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical hit) until it Interacts twice to fix its clothing. Once a creature has had its clothing unraveled, the kikimora can't unravel it further until the target changes clothes.

Kirakor.name: Kirakor
Kirakor.publicNotes:
Kirakors are well-dressed fey musicians, performers, and ambassadors, and as such are often the first fey many commonfolk ever meet. They have a strong sense of conscience and an even greater sense of style, using their dazzling looks to defuse situations before they devolve into combat. However, when fights happen, they stand firm against injustice, even when it's bigger than they are. Kirakors look like bipedal crickets with a full head of humanoid-like hair.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."
